# x86 and MSVC (PC, original Xbox)

Registers: eax return value; eax, ecx, edx scratch; ebx, esi, edi, ebp callee-saved; esp stack.

Calling conventions (read them off the call sites)
- __cdecl: arguments pushed right to left, caller cleans up (`add esp, N` after the call).
- __stdcall: callee cleans up (`ret N`). Win32 API calls.
- __thiscall: MSVC member functions; `this` in ecx, callee cleans up.
- __fastcall: first two arguments in ecx, edx.

Frames: `push ebp; mov ebp, esp; sub esp, N` with locals at [ebp-x] and arguments from [ebp+8]; with
frame-pointer omission (/Oy) everything is esp-relative and offsets shift with each push.

Matching MSVC (versions 4.x-7.1 for older games; the project fixes version and flags)
- /O2 vs /O1 changes idioms (`xor eax, eax`, `rep movsd`, intrinsic `memcpy`/`strlen`).
- Local declaration order and types change stack offsets and register choice.
- `switch` with dense cases becomes `jmp [table + eax*4]`; MSVC also builds byte index tables.
- x87 floating point: `fld`/`fstp`, compares via `fcomp` + `fnstsw ax` + `test ah, 41h`; float to int
  calls `__ftol` (older MSVC) unless the project uses other flags.
- SEH frames (`push -1; push handler; mov eax, fs:[0]`) and `mov [ebp-4], N` state updates come from
  C++ objects with destructors in scope or try/catch.
- Virtual calls: `mov eax, [ecx]; call [eax + off]`.

Annotation-based projects (reccmp) mark functions with comments such as `// FUNCTION: GAME 0x401000`
above each definition; keep them exactly as the project writes them.

x86-64 (64-bit Windows)
- First four integer arguments in rcx, rdx, r8, r9; return in eax/rax; rbx, rbp, rdi, rsi, r12-r15
  callee-saved. 32 bytes of shadow space are reserved by the caller.
- Globals and functions are reached RIP-relative: `mov eax, [rip+disp]`, `call rel32`. The matcher
  normalizes those displacement fields, so writing the same symbol is what makes them match.
- MSVC often uses `lea rax,[rip+...]` for an address and tail-jumps with `jmp` where 32-bit code
  would call and return.

decomp.wtf's Windows matcher
- 32-bit PE has no unwind table: decomp.wtf follows each function's branches to find its end. If an
  older import left a slice without a prologue or `ret` as its own function, `merge_function(name)`
  folds it into the function before it; do that before decompiling the whole thing.
- If a function genuinely can't be reproduced in C/C++ (an MSVC SEH/`fs:` stub, a mid-function entry
  that uses its caller's frame), say why and `retire_function(name, reason)` instead of releasing it
  again: it leaves the queue for good, and the next agent reads your reason.
- Function names come from the executable's symbol table/export names, else `sub_<address>`; rename
  them freely. Referenced data is auto-named `D_<address>` and listed under "Data it uses".
- Globals must be DEFINED in the source or context.h (`int g_counter;`, no `extern`). With `extern`,
  MinGW loads them through a `.refptr` pointer, which is not what the game does. clang-cl is not
  affected, but defining them is still the reliable form.
- Imported functions: declare them `__declspec(dllimport)`, which produces the same call through the
  import table that the game makes. Their slots are named `__imp_<name>`.
- `inspect_binary(function)` asks REA for Ghidra pseudocode, the signature and callers when REA is set
  up; it also returns decomp.wtf's assembly and cross references either way.

Linux programs (ELF, GCC or Clang)
- System V calling convention on x86-64: integer arguments in rdi, rsi, rdx, rcx, r8, r9; floats in
  xmm0-7; return in rax/xmm0; rbx, rbp, r12-r15 callee-saved; no shadow space. 32-bit: cdecl on the stack.
- Function bounds come from the symbol table or .eh_frame, so they are exact even in stripped programs.
- Library calls go through PLT stubs named after the function (`call memcpy`): declare them yourself
  (system headers are not available, so no `std::string` either). `<name>@got` is a library symbol's
  GOT slot, used by code that loads an address through the GOT.
- Non-PIE programs use absolute addresses: `mov edi, 0x4a1230` is a string or global (named `D_`/`STR_`),
  and `jmp [table + rax*8]` is a switch. Position-independent ones use `lea reg, [rip + x]`.
- C++ programs: functions are matched by their mangled names (`_ZN7Archive4OpenEv`). Write the class and
  method so the compiler produces that name; a stripped program's `sub_<address>` can be written inside
  `extern "C" { ... }`, or renamed with rename_symbol to the mangled name you write.
- The compiler version matters as much as with MSVC: the project shows what .comment says built the
  program (for example clang 6.0); the machine's own newer GCC/Clang may not reproduce it exactly.
